name: MSP430F5501IRGZT
title: MSP430F5510 and MSP430F550x: 16-bit ultra-low-power microcontrollers with full-speed USB, 8 KB to 32 KB flash
summary: A family of 16-bit MSP430 microcontrollers (CPUXV2, up to 25 MHz) with a full-speed USB 2.0 device port whose PHY, 3.3-V and 1.8-V regulators and 48-MHz PLL are on chip. Each part has 4 KB of RAM plus 2 KB of USB RAM, four 16-bit timers, a 32-bit multiplier, three DMA channels, RTC, CRC16 and a factory USB bootloader, and runs from 1.8 V to 3.6 V with standby currents near 2 µA. MSP430F5501 has 16 KB of flash, Comparator_B instead of the ADC, one USCI pinned out through port mapping, and 31 I/Os in a 7 mm × 7 mm 48-pin VQFN (RGZ); its siblings change flash size, add the 10-bit ADC, or come in 64-pin VQFN, 48-pin LQFP and 80-ball BGA.
key_figures: 1.8 V to 3.6 V (PMMCOREVx = 0); 2.4 V to 3.6 V for 25 MHz
16 KB, plus 512 B information memory and 2 KB BSL memory
1.55 mA typ at 8 MHz from flash, 3 V (PMMCOREVx = 0)
1.9 µA typ at 2.2 V, 2.1 µA typ at 3 V (XT1, PMMCOREVx = 0, 25°C)
5 µs max from LPM2/3/4 (fast mode, fMCLK ≥ 4 MHz)
Full speed, 8 in + 8 out endpoints, VBUS 3.76 V to 5.5 V, VUSB 3.3 V, 12 mA spare
VQFN-48 RGZ, 7 mm × 7 mm, 250-unit small reel

notes: MSP430F5510CY is the bare die (DIESALE), 0 °C to 70 °C, lead finish from TI on request.

Device nomenclature: MSP = qualified production, XMS = experimental silicon; after the device number, I = –40 °C to 85 °C, then the package code (RGZ, RGC, PT, ZXH, ZQE), then T = small reel, R = large reel, nothing = tube or tray.

operation.text: Eleven 16-bit MSP430 microcontrollers with full-speed USB (PHY, 3.3-V and 1.8-V regulators and PLL on chip). F5510, F5509, F5508 carry a 10-bit ADC and Comparator_B and two USCIs; F5507 to F5504 carry the ADC and one USCI; F5503 to F5500 replace the ADC with Comparator_B. Flash is 32, 24, 16 or 8 KB, RAM 4 KB plus 2 KB of USB RAM. The 64-pin and 80-ball packages give 47 I/Os, the 48-pin packages 31.

16-bit RISC core (CPUXV2) with 16 registers: R0 program counter, R1 stack pointer, R2 status register, R3 constant generator, R4 to R15 general purpose. Register-to-register operations take one clock. 51 original instructions in three formats with seven addressing modes for the source and four for the destination, plus extended-address instructions; each works on bytes or words. Peripherals sit on the data, address and control buses and are reached by every instruction.

One active mode and six low-power modes, entered by software; any interrupt wakes the part, runs its handler and can return it to the low-power mode. LPM0: CPU and MCLK off, ACLK, SMCLK and FLL on. LPM1: as LPM0 with the FLL off. LPM2: MCLK, FLL and DCOCLK off, DCO DC generator still on, ACLK on. LPM3: as LPM2 with the DCO generator off too. LPM4: ACLK off and crystal stopped, all data kept. LPM4.5: regulator off, no data kept, woken from RST/NMI, P1 or P2.
Vectors and the reset address live from 0FFFFh down to 0FF80h; each holds the 16-bit address of its handler. Reset has the top priority (63), then system NMI and user NMI.

Every device ships with the USB BSL, which can program flash or RAM over USB behind a user password. It needs RST/NMI/SBWTDIO, PU.0/DP, PU.1/DM, PUR, VBUS and VSSU, plus the normal USB parts (a suitable XT2 crystal and decoupling). After a BOR the BSL reads PUR: if it is held high, the BSL starts. So PUR must be low after BOR whenever the BSL is not wanted, even in designs that never use USB; a 1-MΩ pull-down is recommended.
A UART BSL can replace the factory USB BSL in BSL memory. It uses RST/NMI/SBWTDIO and TEST/SBWTCK for the entry sequence, P1.1 to transmit and P1.2 to receive, plus VCC and VSS.

Four-wire JTAG uses PJ.3/TCK, PJ.2/TMS, PJ.1/TDI/TCLK and PJ.0/TDO, shared with port J; TEST/SBWTCK switches the pins to JTAG and RST/NMI/SBWTDIO is also needed by the tools. Two-wire Spy-Bi-Wire uses TEST/SBWTCK as clock and RST/NMI/SBWTDIO as data. TEST has an internal pull-down of 60 kΩ typical.

Programmable through JTAG, Spy-Bi-Wire, the BSL or by the CPU in system, in bytes, words or long words. Main memory is n segments of 512 bytes; information memory is segments A to D of 128 bytes. Main segments erase one by one or all together; A to D erase one by one or with main memory. Segment A has its own lock. No external programming voltage is needed.

RAM is in sectors (2 KB each, see the memory map). Each sector can be powered off to cut leakage, losing its data, and drops into a low-power retention state by itself when it can. USB RAM works as ordinary RAM when USB is not used.

Up to six 8-bit ports. 64-pin parts have full P1, P2, P4 and P6, P5 with 6 bits and P3 with 5 bits; 48-pin parts have P6 with 4 bits, P2 with 1 bit and no P3. Port J has four bits on every device. Each bit is set up on its own: direction, pull-up or pull-down, drive strength. Every bit of P1 and P2 has an edge-selectable interrupt and can wake the part from LPM4.5. Ports are read byte-wide (P1 to P6) or word-wide in pairs (PA to PC).

A mapping controller routes digital functions to any pin of port P4. Each P4MAPx register takes a value from the mnemonic table; 0 is no function, 31 (written 0FFh) is analog with driver and input buffer off. After reset P4.0 to P4.5 carry USCI_B1 and USCI_A1 and P4.6, P4.7 carry nothing. On 48-pin parts the second USCI reaches pins only through this mapping.

The Unified Clock System has a 32-kHz watch-crystal oscillator XT1 (LF mode only; XT1 HF mode is not supported), a very-low-power oscillator VLO, a trimmed 32768-Hz reference REFO, a DCO, and a high-frequency crystal oscillator XT2 (4 MHz to 32 MHz). An FLL with a modulator locks the DCO to a set multiple of the chosen reference; the DCO is up and stable in under 5 µs. ACLK, MCLK (CPU) and SMCLK (peripherals) can each come from XT1, XT2, VLO, REFO or DCO; ACLK is also brought out divided by 1 to 32.

An on-chip regulator makes the core supply VCORE at one of four levels set by PMMCOREVx (1.40 V to 1.90 V typical); higher levels allow faster MCLK but need a higher VCC (8 MHz from 1.8 V, 12 MHz from 2.0 V, 20 MHz from 2.2 V, 25 MHz from 2.4 V). VCORE needs 470 nF to ground and the DVCC capacitance must be at least ten times it. Brownout reset handles power-up and power-down. Supply supervisors (SVS, which reset the part) and monitors (SVM, which only flag) watch both DVCC and VCORE against software-chosen levels.

AVCC and DVCC should come from the same source; up to 0.3 V between them is tolerated during power-up and running. All grounds (AVSS, DVSS1, DVSS2) are at 0 V. VCORE and V18 are internal supplies: nothing but their capacitors may be connected. The exposed pad of the QFN packages goes to VSS.
MPY32 multiplies 8-, 16-, 24- and 32-bit operands, signed or unsigned, with or without accumulate.

RTC_A runs as a 32-bit counter or as a calendar clock with month-length and leap-year handling, alarms and offset calibration. In counter mode it also has two 8-bit timers that can be chained into 16 bits.
WDT_A resets the system when its interval runs out without service; it can instead serve as an interval timer giving periodic interrupts.

SYS handles power-on reset and power-up clear, NMI source selection, the reset and NMI vector generators (SYSRSTIV, SYSSNIV, SYSUNIV), bootloader entry and the device descriptors, and offers a JTAG mailbox for data exchange with a debugger.

Three DMA channels move data between addresses without the CPU, for example from ADC10_A results to RAM, so the CPU can stay asleep. Triggers come from timers, USCIs, the ADC, USB, the multiplier, other channels or the DMAE0 pin.

Each USCI has an A part (UART, enhanced UART with automatic baud detection, IrDA, 3- or 4-pin SPI) and a B part (3- or 4-pin SPI, I2C). F5510, F5509 and F5508 have two USCIs, F5507 to F5500 one; on the 48-pin packages USCI functions reach pins through the port P4 mapping controller.

TA0 is a 16-bit Timer_A with five capture/compare registers, TA1 and TA2 Timer_A with three each, TB0 a 16-bit Timer_B with seven. All do capture, compare, PWM and interval timing with interrupts on overflow and on each register. TB0 reaches pins only through the port mapping controller.
An analog comparator for slope-type A/D conversion, battery supervision and watching external signals; up to 8 inputs (4 on 48-pin parts) with an internal 32-tap reference ladder.

A 10-bit SAR converter with sample control, reference generator, result buffer and a window comparator raising three interrupt flags. Channel 10 is the temperature sensor and channel 11 half of AVCC. An external reference on VeREF needs 10 µF and 100 nF decoupling.
CRC16 forms a CRC-CCITT signature over data written to it. The shared REF module provides 1.5-V, 2.0-V and 2.5-V references for the analog peripherals.

A full-speed USB 2.0 device with control, interrupt and bulk transfers, eight input and eight output endpoints, its own LDOs, PHY and PLL. The 3.3-V LDO runs from VBUS (3.76 V to 5.5 V) and outputs VUSB, which can also feed up to 12 mA to the board; V18 is internal. Recommended capacitors: 4.7 µF on VBUS, 220 nF on VUSB, 220 nF on V18. D+ and D- take 27-Ω series resistors; PUR with an external resistor to D+ forms the USB pull-up. USB needs MCLK of at least 1.5 MHz, and the PLL needs PMMCOREVx ≥ 2. A PLL reference of 1.5 MHz to 3 MHz gives 48 MHz.
The EEM (S version) gives three triggers or breakpoints on memory access, one on a CPU register write, up to four combined into complex triggers, a cycle counter and module-level clock control.

Keep crystal traces short, put a ground plane round the oscillator pins, keep other clock and data lines from coupling into them, route nothing under or next to XIN/XOUT or XT2IN/XT2OUT, avoid assembly materials that load these pins, and make sure any conformal coating adds no leakage between them. XT1 has internal load capacitors selectable at about 1, 5.5, 8.5 and 12 pF; XT2 needs external capacitors.

RST/NMI/SBWTDIO is an active-low reset with its internal pull-up enabled by default in reset mode; a low pulse of at least 2 µs resets the part. The same pin can be the NMI input or the Spy-Bi-Wire data line.
